name: Minefield

scoring.report_note: Report pair-level deltas only. Never rank individuals — the crossing measures the pair's trust loop, not courage.

description: Two-minute pre/post measure for the Minefield trust exercise. Scores at pair level: how did clarity under responsibility, trusting on voice alone, and using the stop word change across the two crossings?

instructions.pre: Before pairing up. Each participant answers alone, about their own last week at work — not about the exercise.
instructions.post: Immediately after the debrief. Same items, now answered about both crossings, as a pair.

items.pre_text: When I am responsible for someone, my instructions get clearer.
items.post_text: As navigator, responsibility made our instructions clearer.

items.pre_text: I can act on a colleague's word without seeing the situation myself.
items.post_text: As walker, we acted on the voice without seeing the course.

items.pre_text: Under pressure I talk faster instead of clearer.
items.post_text: When the walker wobbled, the instructions got faster, not clearer.

items.pre_text: I stop and ask before a risky step, even when it slows things down.
items.post_text: The stop word (or the wish we had used it) showed up in our crossing.

items.pre_text: Being responsible for someone's outcome weighs on me more than my own.
items.post_text: After swapping roles, being the navigator was the harder side of trust.

items.pre_text: After a miscommunication, I rebuild the channel before continuing.
items.post_text: After our near-miss, we changed how we talked — then kept walking.

report.title: Minefield — pair trust delta
sections: Near-miss collection: one moment per pair, blame-free
One suggested navigation habit per pair, derived from the largest positive delta
